name: NAGAYA Aoyama
card: A quiet 2nd floor in Minami-Aoyama with a wooden terrace of about 70 m²
title: NAGAYA Aoyama — a shared office with a 70 m² wooden terrace and 29 private rooms on the 2nd floor of Grancasa Minami-Aoyama
lead: NAGAYA Aoyama is on the 2nd floor of Grancasa Minami-Aoyama, an eight-minute walk from Omotesando Station. Its concept is “a quiet working environment, achievable even in the city centre”. It has an 18-seat open space, 29 private rooms, four meeting rooms and an outdoor wooden terrace of about 70 m². Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Omotesando Station 8 min walk / Nogizaka Station 9 min / Gaienmae Station 11 min
18-seat open space / 29 private rooms / 4 meeting rooms / outdoor wooden terrace (about 70 m²) / phone room
concept: Quiet in the city centre
NAGAYA Aoyama's concept is “a quiet working environment, achievable even in the city centre”. It is in Minami-Aoyama, eight minutes on foot from Omotesando Station.
Twenty-nine private rooms, an 18-seat open space, four meeting rooms and an outdoor wooden terrace are all gathered on the same 2nd floor.
steps: Past reception is the 18-seat open space.
The open-space “Full-time A” membership is ¥19,800 a month.
A table in the open space
There are 29 private rooms; dedicated private-room memberships range from ¥55,000 to ¥154,000 a month.
There are also private booths for working quietly alone.
There is an outdoor wooden terrace of about 70 m².
It is a place to eat lunch outside or work somewhere different for a change.
There are four meeting rooms, including ones for 6 and 4.
A phone room lets members without a private room take calls too.

word.title: What is a nagaya?
body: A traditional Japanese row house: several homes lined up side by side under one roof. Residents lived on either side of shared walls and met in the alleys and around the well.
NAGAYA Aoyama is likewise made up of rows of private rooms and shared areas. The origin of the name is being confirmed with the operator.

name: Soil work Nihonbashi 1st
card: Windows facing a park, with a café-bakery on the ground floor
title: Soil work Nihonbashi 1st — coworking and a cooperative office with park-facing windows in Nihonbashi Kobunacho
lead: Soil work Nihonbashi 1st is on the 6th floor of a building in Nihonbashi Kobunacho. One floor is coworking, and the floor above is a cooperative office shared by a variety of tenants. The official website says its park-facing windows let you sense the passing of the day and the seasons, even in the city centre. On the ground floor is the café-bakery PARKLET. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Mitsukoshimae Station about 6 min walk / Ningyocho Station about 7 min
Coworking (lounge, group and fixed-desk memberships) / offices (private units) / meeting rooms / phone booths / shared kitchen
concept: Windows facing a park
Soil work Nihonbashi 1st has one floor of coworking, with a cooperative office above it shared by a variety of tenants.
The official website highlights the park-facing windows, through which you can sense the passing of the day and the seasons. On the ground floor is the café-bakery PARKLET.
steps: Membership types are lounge, group and fixed-desk.
It is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and company registration is available.
There are meeting rooms and phone booths.
A shared kitchen also lets you prepare meals.
A park is just a short walk away.
Together with PARKLET, the café-bakery on the ground floor, the whole building connects with the neighbourhood.

word.title: What is a cooperative office?
body: An office where several companies or tenants gather in one building and use it together. At Soil work Nihonbashi 1st, the floor above the coworking space is a cooperative office.
It is a format that makes it easy for people in the same building to connect.

name: FARO Aoyama
card: A shared office of 100% Japanese timber, wrapped in greenery
title: FARO Aoyama — a design-led shared office of Japanese wood and greenery, five minutes from Gaienmae and Aoyama-itchome
lead: FARO Aoyama is in Minami-Aoyama 2-chome, a five-minute walk from Gaienmae and Aoyama-itchome stations. It opened in 2013. The official website calls it “a shared office that combines design and comfort”, describing an office space built with 100% Japanese timber and wrapped in greenery. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Gaienmae and Aoyama-itchome stations, 5 min walk
Small offices (fully private rooms for about 1–10) / free-address shared seats and members' lounge / gallery space (B1F, 36 m²) / rooftop terrace / phone booths
hero_cap: Free desks and the members' lounge
concept: Japanese wood and greenery
FARO Aoyama uses 100% Japanese timber. The official website describes an office wrapped in greenery, where you can feel the warmth of natural materials and a sense of living alongside nature.
It opened in 2013 as “a shared office that combines design and comfort”, and has underfloor heating.
steps: The free-address shared seats double as the members' lounge, at ¥22,000 a month.
There is a kitchenette and kitchen, three multifunction printers and phone booths.
Free desks and the members' lounge
Small offices are fully private rooms for about 1–10 people.
The shared lounge and team rooms are in the same building.
The rooftop terrace was renovated in 2024.
On the basement floor is a 36 m² gallery space.

word.title: What is free address?
body: A way of working with no assigned seat: you use whichever seat is free. At FARO Aoyama, the free-address seats double as the members' lounge.
You can change where you sit to suit your mood or work that day.

name: Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi
card: A free start-up support centre for people just beginning to think about starting a business
title: Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi — the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's free start-up support centre for anyone wondering “should I start a business?”
lead: Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi is on the ground floor of the Meiji Yasuda Life Building in Marunouchi. Part of TOKYO Startup Station, it supports people who have started to wonder “should I start a business?”. A lounge for working and meetings, start-up advice from concierges who are entrepreneurs themselves, events almost every day, and a kids' room staffed by childcare workers — every service is free. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi (TOKYO Startup Station)
Lounge (1,500+ books on starting a business) / start-up consultations (concierge, by reservation) / events / kids' room (childcare by qualified staff, by reservation)
Member registration required; all services free
concept: When you start wondering “should I start a business?”

The official website presents this place as a start-up support centre for people who have begun to wonder whether to start a business. It handles a wide range of questions, from first interest through to preparation.
All it takes is an online member application, and there is no charge. It is designed as an entrance anyone can walk into, even before deciding to start a business.
steps: Events useful for starting a business are held almost every day.
Resident community managers help members share information with one another.
There is a kids' room where qualified childcare workers look after children (by reservation).
It makes it easier for parents to join consultations and events.

word.title: What is a start-up support centre?
body: A facility that supports people about to start a business or who have just started one. Many offer advice and seminars as well as space.
Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi offers consultations, events, its lounge, childcare and books, all free.

credits: © TOKYO Startup Station (official website: “Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi”)
TOKYO Startup Station official website: “Startup Hub Tokyo Marunouchi”

name: NEXs Tokyo Community Space
card: A members' space in Marunouchi connecting start-ups from across Japan and Tokyo
title: NEXs Tokyo Community Space — a free members' base in Marunouchi connecting start-ups from across Japan and Tokyo
lead: The NEXs Tokyo Community Space is on the 4th floor of the Shin-Tokyo Building in Marunouchi. It is a base where start-ups from regions across Japan and from Tokyo connect with players at home and abroad. There is LIVE PARK seating 80, Xs BAR for 8, WORK STUDIO for 20 and a RADIO STATION for broadcasting, all free for registered members. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: LIVE PARK (80 seated full / 40 half) / Xs BAR (8) / WORK STUDIO (20) / RADIO STATION (2–4) / free-address seats and meeting rooms
Registered start-up, partner and mentor members; free (company registration not available). Start-ups generally for 18 months
concept: Connecting Japan's regions and Tokyo, at home and abroad

The official website describes it as a base where start-ups from across Japan's regions and from Tokyo connect organically with players at home and abroad, offering fast-moving information sharing and a flexible work environment.
One floor takes on four roles: a place to share information, to work, to do business and to hold events.
steps: LIVE PARK seats 80 when used in full, or 40 in half.
When no event is on, it serves as a place to gather and share information.
WORK STUDIO seats 20, with free-address seats, Wi-Fi and power.
A multifunction printer is available (charged separately).
Xs BAR seats 8 and suits business talks and small meetings.
There are also meeting rooms and workshop space.
RADIO STATION is a broadcasting space for 2–4 people. For public broadcasts, around 20 people can gather around it.
Start-ups can share what they are doing with the outside world, right there.

word.title: What is a mentor?
body: Someone who supports another person's growth with advice drawn from their own experience and knowledge.
As well as start-up members, partner and mentor members can also use the NEXs Tokyo Community Space free of charge.

name: Chiyoda Platform Square
card: A shared office reborn from a ward public building, running since 2004
title: Chiyoda Platform Square — a shared office in a renovated Chiyoda City public building, connecting generations and regions
lead: Chiyoda Platform Square is in Kanda-Nishikicho, a two-minute walk from Takebashi Station. Born in 2004 as a pioneer of coworking and shared-office culture in Japan, it was created by renovating a Chiyoda City public building. It has free-address “Open Nest” seating, lockable “Closed Nest” units, meeting rooms that can host talks for 200 people, and a rooftop garden. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Platform Service Co., Ltd. (a non-profit-type company)
Open Nest (free address) / Closed Nest (private units of about 3.4–53 m²) / meeting rooms (B1F, 4F, 5F) / lobby, wooden deck, rooftop garden
concept: A shared office where generations and regions connect and grow
The official website presents it as “a shared office where many generations and regions connect and grow” — a base where people of different ages and places create new business and culture together.
It was born in 2004 as a pioneer of Japan's coworking and shared-office culture, by renovating a Chiyoda City public building.
steps: A bright lounge beside a café
Through the entrance, a bright, open lounge welcomes you. A café next door makes it handy for meeting up or quick discussions.
Beside the main building is a wooden deck surrounded by greenery, used for meetings and community events.
Pick a seat to suit the day
Open Nest is a free-address workspace where you choose a seat to suit your mood or task that day.
With just a laptop, you can start work straight away.
Closed Nest units are lockable private workplaces, ranging from about 3.4 m² to 53 m².
Landlines are available, and security is at a level that supports gaining Japan's PrivacyMark certification.
Meeting rooms on B1F, 4F and 5F handle everything from internal meetings to talks for around 200 people.
A rooftop garden for tenants only even has a vegetable patch.

word.title: What is a non-profit-type company?
body: A company that takes the form of a joint-stock company but does not aim to pay out profits as dividends, instead using its results for the local community and society.
Chiyoda Platform Square is run by Platform Service Co., Ltd., a non-profit-type company.

name: StartupSide Tokyo
card: 50 seats and 8 private rooms, with incubation managers on site
title: StartupSide Tokyo — an entrepreneur support centre on two floors in Suidobashi, with 50 coworking seats and 8 private rooms
lead: StartupSide Tokyo is on the 8th and 9th floors of VORT Suidobashi III, a five-minute walk from Suidobashi Station. An incubation facility that aims to raise the “start-up quality” of entrepreneurs, it has 50 coworking seats for networking and events on the 9th floor, and eight private rooms for 2–6, meeting rooms and online booths on the 8th. It is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and community managers and incubation managers support entrepreneurs. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 9F: 50 coworking seats, reception / 8F: 8 private rooms (2–6 people, 4.0–11.9 m²), meeting rooms, online booths
concept: Raising start-up quality
The official website states its aim of raising entrepreneurs' “start-up quality”, which it defines as the rates of starting, continuing and scaling a business.
Community managers and incubation managers provide ongoing support for members' business growth.
steps: A floor for networking and events
The 9th floor holds reception and the coworking space. There is room for networking and events, with a desk-work area at the back.
It is set up as a place to meet people who create innovation together.
At the back of the coworking space is a desk-work area for focused work.
Wi-Fi and power are free, and printers and lockers are available.
The 8th floor has private rooms, meeting rooms and online booths. Private rooms include ones for 3 and for 5 (with a window).
Private-room members can also use the 9th-floor coworking space free of charge.

word.title: What is an incubation manager?
body: A support person who helps entrepreneurs' businesses grow — giving advice and connecting them with experts and support schemes.
At StartupSide Tokyo, community managers and incubation managers support entrepreneurs.

credits: © Tsukurie Co., Ltd. (StartupSide Tokyo official website: “Floor map”)

name: City Lab Tokyo
card: An open-innovation base in Kyobashi for building sustainable cities
title: City Lab Tokyo — an open-innovation base for sustainable urban development, directly linked to Kyobashi Station
lead: City Lab Tokyo is on the 6th floor of Tokyo Square Garden, directly linked to Exit 3 of Kyobashi Station. Opened in 2018, it is a participatory platform aiming to create business for sustainable urban development. Its roughly 300 m² space uses natural materials in the interior with the environment in mind. Through running coworking and event spaces, it fosters connections between people working towards sustainable cities. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Directly linked to Kyobashi Station Exit 3
About 300 m²: meeting room, salon, long table (up to about 120 seated when meeting room and salon are combined)
concept: An Open Innovation Platform for sustainable cities and society
The official website describes it as “an Open Innovation Platform for building sustainable cities and society”.
Opened in Kyobashi in 2018, it builds networks and collaboration towards sustainable cities by running coworking and event spaces and planning a range of programmes.
steps: A space built with natural materials
The roughly 300 m² space uses natural materials in its interior, with the environment in mind.
It adapts to solo work, workshops and standing meetings.
A room that also hosts seminars
The meeting room and salon each have a projector, wireless microphone and Blu-ray player.
With the meeting room and salon combined, it seats up to about 120 people.

word.title: What is a sustainable city?
body: A city that keeps environmental, economic and social needs in balance so people can go on living there well into the future.
City Lab Tokyo works on building networks and encouraging collaboration towards sustainable cities.

name: CASE Shinjuku
card: One minute from Takadanobaba Station, where creators and entrepreneurs loosely connect
title: CASE Shinjuku — a shared office connecting creators, engineers and entrepreneurs, one minute from Takadanobaba Station
lead: CASE Shinjuku is on the 4th floor of the Sankei Building, a one-minute walk from Takadanobaba Station. Under the motto “broaden, deepen and change your world in an office with loose connections”, it creates a place where creators, engineers, entrepreneurs and business owners connect. There is coworking with an open interior, a members-only shared office, private rooms of about 10 m² and an event space, and you can also consult certified SME advisers on financing and more. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Coworking space / shared office (individual booths or shared use) / private office (about 10 m²) / event space
Consultations, including on financing, with certified SME advisers and others / company registration (address use)
Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00 (closed Sundays and holidays; shared office 24 hours)
concept: An office with loose connections
The official website carries the motto “broaden, deepen and change your world in an office with loose connections”.

It positions itself as “a place where creators, engineers, entrepreneurs and business owners connect”, aiming for an environment where people in different lines of work naturally get to know each other.
steps: An open space that also hosts study sessions
The coworking space has an open, airy interior.
Study sessions and events can be held here too.
The members-only shared office can be used as individual booths or shared by a small team.
The shared office is available 24 hours a day.
A private room of about 10 m²
There are self-contained private offices of about 10 m².
Company registration (address use) is also available.

word.title: What is a shared office?
body: A workplace where several companies or individuals share one office.
CASE Shinjuku's shared office is for members only and can be used as individual booths or shared by a team.

name: Shinagawa Industry Support and Exchange Facility SHIP
card: A members' lounge and a 3D-printer workshop in Osaki, run for Shinagawa City
title: SHIP (Shinagawa Industry Support and Exchange Facility) — a members' lounge and a workshop with 3D printers in Osaki
lead: SHIP, the Shinagawa Industry Support and Exchange Facility, is on the 3rd and 4th floors of Osaki Bright Core, an eight-minute walk from Osaki Station. In the Shinagawa, Osaki and Gotanda area, where manufacturing companies cluster, it is a base where engineers, designers and entrepreneurs meet companies large and small. It has a monthly-membership open lounge, a workshop with 3D printers and laser cutters, rental meeting rooms and offices, and marked its 10th anniversary on 1 June 2025. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: SHIP (Shinagawa Industry Support and Exchange Facility)
Members' open lounge (4F) / maker workshop (3D printers, laser cutters) / rental meeting rooms / multipurpose room / offices
Monthly membership ¥8,800–¥27,500 / one-time membership ¥550 per hour
concept: Helping bring next-generation devices and services to life

The official website explains that, in an area where major manufacturers and their suppliers gather, SHIP serves as a hub where start-ups, small and medium firms and large companies meet, helping realise next-generation devices and services.
As of May 2025 it had 208 member companies, with information and communications the largest group at 38.1%, followed by academic research and professional services, and manufacturing.
steps: The 4th-floor open lounge is a coworking space with monthly membership. You can sit anywhere in the facility.
Seats at the back of the lounge are set aside for web meetings.
Seats at the back of the lounge
A space with greenery and light
The café area is where you can eat and drink.
The sofa area, filled with greenery and light, works for meetings or a change of pace.
There are focus seats you can use for up to four hours a day.
Bookable four-person booths suit business talks and meetings.
The workshop has several 3D printers for different uses and a laser cutter.
There is a range of tools, and advice on making things is free.

word.title: What is a designated manager?
body: An organisation entrusted by a city or ward to manage and run a public facility on its behalf.
SHIP is run by a designated manager.

credits: SHIP (Shinagawa Industry Support and Exchange Facility)
